Website review · prepared for Quinten de Graaf · 27 November 2026

degraafconsultingservices.com.au

Thirty years of real hospitality experience, on a website that doesn't show it yet.

By Nicole Pezza, Pezza MediaPages reviewed: Home, About, Services, Projects, Contact

The short version

You've opened and fixed venues for some of the biggest names in Australian hospitality. A visitor landing on your site today wouldn't know that. The headline could belong to any consultant, the copy reads like early AI writing from 2023, there isn't a single review, and a booking popup asks for their time before they know who you are. The good news is that every one of these is fixable, and most of the fixes are words, not a rebuild.

Say what you doOne plain first line: who you help and how.
Show the proofReviews, your story and a result for every project.
Earn the callPopup later, one clear button, and say what they get.
Fix first costs you enquiries now Fix soon weakens trust Quick fix under an hour

What I found, and how I'd fix it

First impression

The first line doesn't say what you do

Fix first
What I see
The headline is Your Partner in Hospitality Growth. It's friendly, but it doesn't say whether you design venues, fix struggling ones, train staff or do the books.
Why it matters
People decide in a few seconds whether they're in the right place. If they have to scroll to find out, many won't.
The fix
Open with who you help and what you do for them, in plain words. A rewrite is in the samples below.

The copy reads like early AI writing

Fix first
What I see
Lines like excellence, innovation, and integrity, achieve greatness, 360-degree support and Take Your Hospitality Business to the Next Level, some of them repeated across pages.
Why it matters
Readers now spot this style instantly, and it makes a real expert sound like a template. It also hides everything that makes you different.
The fix
Write in your voice, in the first person, with specifics: the brands, the problems, what changed. Every claim should be something only you could say.

The layout is hard to follow, and the photo feels distant

Fix soon
What I see
The home page jumps between services, projects, a blog and forms, with no clear path through it. The main photo feels formal and a little cold for a business built on relationships.
Why it matters
Consulting is bought on trust. People want to feel they know you before they pick up the phone.
The fix
One simple story from top to bottom (see the page flow below) and a warmer, more relaxed photo, ideally of you on the floor of a venue.

Trust and proof

There are no reviews anywhere

Fix first
What I see
Client logos, but not one testimonial on any page.
Why it matters
Logos show who you've worked with. Reviews show they'd hire you again. For a consultant, that's the difference between interesting and trusted.
The fix
Ask three to five past clients for two or three sentences each, with their name, role and venue. Put one near the top and the rest beside the projects.

Your own story is missing

Fix first
What I see
30+ years is almost all we learn about you. We don't hear which businesses you've run, what you've turned around or why operators call you.
Why it matters
You are the product. Your track record is the strongest selling point on the site, and right now it's a single number.
The fix
A short, human About section: where you started, the brands you've worked inside, two or three problems you've solved and how you like to work.

Projects are store names with no outcome

Fix soon
What I see
Entries like Oporto Gladesville and Red Rooster Dalby, with nothing about the brief or the result. The Load More button doesn't load anything.
Why it matters
A name tells a visitor you were there. A result tells them what you could do for them.
The fix
Turn each project into a three-line case study: the challenge, what you did, what changed (opened on time, back to profit, sales up). Add a photo of the finished venue.

A tyre chain sits in the hospitality line-up

Quick fix
What I see
Bob Jane T-Marts appears among the client logos directly under Trusted by Leading Hospitality Brands.
The fix
Move it to a separate "other industries" line, or leave it out, so the hospitality message stays sharp.

Getting the call

The booking popup appears too early

Fix first
What I see
A free-session popup appears before a visitor has read anything about you.
Why it matters
Asking for someone's time before they understand what you offer feels pushy, and most people close it without reading.
The fix
Show it only once someone has scrolled past your proof, or when they're about to leave. Better still, make the call the main button on the page and drop the popup.

The free call isn't explained

Fix first
What I see
Get a free 15-minute session! and nothing else. Who is it for, what happens on the call, what do they leave with?
The fix
One or two lines that promise a clear result, for example "Tell me what's not working and leave with your top three fixes." A rewrite is in the samples below.

Too many buttons, all saying different things

Fix soon
What I see
Around 25 buttons on the home page: Get In Touch, Know More, Learn More, View More, View All, Schedule your appointment. The contact form also asks for "Name", "URL" or "Company" depending on the page.
The fix
One main action everywhere, "Book a free 15-minute call", and one contact form used on every page.

Six services with equal weight, and no "how it works"

Fix soon
What I see
Coaching, design and construction, finance, strategy, turnarounds and operations all sit side by side, and nothing explains what working with you actually looks like.
The fix
Lead with the one or two services that match your new direction, then add a simple three-step "how it works": free call, on-site review, plan and support.

Name and housekeeping

The old name is still everywhere

Fix first
What I see
"Sixth Sense Consulting" still appears in:
  • the page titles for Home, Services and Contact, which is what Google shows
  • the preview text and image when the site is shared
  • the first email address on every page
  • the Instagram and YouTube handles, and the map link
  • the hidden labels on the client logos
Why it matters
Google and new visitors see two businesses, which splits your search ranking and makes people wonder which one is real.
The fix
A one-off clean-up so every title, preview, email and handle says De Graaf Consulting.

The blog stopped in May 2025

Fix soon
What I see
The latest posts are from April and May 2025.
Why it matters
A blog that stopped 18 months ago makes the business look inactive, which is the opposite of what you want.
The fix
Either hide it, or bring it back with one useful, search-friendly article a month on the questions operators actually ask (opening costs, menu pricing, turning around a slow venue).

Small errors that are easy to fix

Quick fix
  • The Outlook address is spelt deraaf instead of degraaf, and doesn't match your website domain.
  • The booking widget still shows a slot from Wednesday 30 April 2025.
  • Typos and stray capitals: OUR Services, Why Our clients prefer Us, Faq.
  • US and Australian spelling are mixed (customizes and prioritize next to optimise and analysed).

What the fixes could sound like

Draft copy to show the direction. The details would come from you.

The first screen

Now

Your Partner in Hospitality Growth. 30+ Years of Experience | Trusted by Leading Hospitality Brands Across Australia.

Could be

Hospitality consulting for restaurants, cafes and QSR chains across Australia. 30 years of opening, fixing and growing venues for brands like Oporto, Red Rooster and The Coffee Club.

The free call

Now

Get a free 15-minute session!

Could be

Book a free 15-minute call. Tell me what's not working in your venue, and you'll leave with your top three fixes, whether or not we work together.

A service

Now

Turnaround & Transformation, delivered with excellence, innovation and integrity. Know More.

Could be

Turnarounds. Sales slipping, costs creeping up, staff turning over? I come in, find what's really going wrong and stay until the numbers move.

A simpler home page

One story, top to bottom, with the same button at every step.

  1. What you doThe plain first line, a warm photo and the "Book a free call" button.
  2. ProofClient logos with one strong review right underneath.
  3. ServicesYour one or two lead services, each in two or three plain sentences.
  4. How it worksFree call, on-site review, plan and support.
  5. ResultsThree short case studies with photos and outcomes.
  6. About QuintenYour story and why operators call you.
  7. Book the callWhat they'll get from the 15 minutes, and the booking calendar.

Where I'd start

This week

  • Fix the email spelling and the April 2025 booking slot
  • Change every "Sixth Sense" title, preview and handle
  • Move or remove the booking popup
  • Ask three past clients for a review

The refresh

  • A new first screen and home page in your own voice
  • A proper About section and service pages
  • Projects rewritten as short case studies
  • A blog plan, or a clean exit from it
